info.title: Chief Local Workspace Tools
info.description: Private runtime-local capabilities composed for Chief workspace agents.

post.summary: Create an action that genuinely requires the user
post.description: Use only for work the user must personally decide or perform. Recording an action never completes the current task.

post.summary: Save a normalized analytics dataset
post.description: Stores a bounded reusable analytics projection from a connected source.

get.summary: List schedules and their approval state

post.summary: Propose recurring or one-time agent work for user approval
post.description: Configure the complete scheduled team: lead agentId, collaborators, instructions, optional outcome/constraints/run limit, and a cron, onceAt or webhook trigger. Set newChannel to {} to create a mission channel automatically, or provide its name and inviteUserIds. Otherwise use conversationId; missing teammates are added with membership permission. Supply timezone and optionally skipDates. Use a stable id to revise a proposal. The user must approve the latest proposal before execution; webhook triggers are connected through workspace Webhooks settings.

post.summary: Open or navigate Chief's embedded browser
post.description: Opens an HTTP or HTTPS page in the visible interactive browser. Reserve this for interaction, authentication, screenshots, or user takeover; use web_read for ordinary public research. A server started on this computer is reachable at localhost on its chosen port; port 8080 is reserved for the computer control API. The browser continues its current session by default; use fresh=true only when the task requires a clean session.

post.summary: Inspect Chief's visible embedded browser page
post.description: Returns the current URL, title, readable text, and visible semantic controls. Re-inspect after navigation or a material page change.

post.summary: Close Chief's embedded browser
post.description: Ends the current embedded browser run after its work is genuinely finished. Never close a browser after handing it to the user for sign-in, consent, MFA, or another human action.

post.summary: Change the embedded browser presentation
post.description: Keeps the browser inline by default. Use picture-in-picture only when the user asks to snap or minimize the live browser, or when an explicit handoff calls for it.

post.summary: Click an agent-browser ref or visible control
post.description: Clicks the first matching current agent-browser snapshot ref or semantic label and returns the refreshed page snapshot. Prefer the exact @ref from the latest snapshot, including for radio-style option cards.

post.summary: Fill a visible browser field by label
post.description: Fills a non-secret visible field in Chief's embedded browser. Never request or fill passwords, passkeys, MFA codes, or account credentials; the user handles authentication directly.

post.summary: Choose an option in a visible browser select field
post.description: Selects one or more values from a native select control using a current agent-browser ref or semantic label. Prefer this over keyboard navigation for select fields.

post.summary: Press a key in the visible browser
post.description: Presses a key such as Enter or Escape in the shared agent-browser session. Do not traverse controls with repeated Tab or arrow presses when the current snapshot exposes a clickable @ref.

post.summary: Publish a message or thread reply
post.description: Publishes deliberate user-facing content into a shared channel. Address people and agents with @Name and include their principal IDs in mentions. Channel members.list returns each person's name, role, and id. Never invent a @chief (user) tag. To present work, first create or revise it with files.write (or publish binary media), then pass its file ID in artifactIds. This inserts clickable cards opening those artifacts in this channel’s Canvas. Only artifacts belonging to this channel can be attached. Ordinary agent working output is private and does not appear in the channel.

post.summary: Run Git against the agent computer repository
Save an image, video, audio, PDF, or other file to the workspace Files library
post.description: Publish an existing file up to 8 MB. Use a /workspace-relative path, a filename with its extension, and the matching MIME type. The output persists in Files and can be previewed or downloaded by workspace members.

get.summary: List documents and published media visible to you in this workspace

post.summary: Read a workspace document or published media metadata
Create or revise a workspace document
post.description: Saves a versioned document in the current conversation. For revisions, pass the file's version as expectedVersionId, converted to a string. For interactive artifacts use format html with a self-contained HTML document, inline CSS and JavaScript, no external libraries or network calls. Use format csv or json for structured data. After saving, call channels.messages.post with artifactIds containing the file ID to place a Canvas card in chat. Use computer.artifacts.publish for existing images, PDFs, recordings, and other binary files.

post.summary: Start Google Analytics authorization
Complete and verify Google Analytics authorization
Select and verify a Google Analytics property
Begin user-owned Google OAuth client setup
Securely capture and store a Google OAuth client
Open a secure local connection handoff
post.description: Opens an Executor connection or OAuth-client handoff in Chief's embedded browser with local authentication added by the trusted host. Use only in a user-started integration setup run.

post.summary: Securely capture a generated provider credential
post.description: Call only while the provider is displaying a newly generated credential in Chief's embedded browser. Chief captures it inside the trusted host and stores it in the prepared Executor connection without returning the value.

post.summary: Open an integration provider page with automatic resume
post.description: Opens a page belonging to the active integration. If provider authentication is required, Chief resumes this same setup agent automatically when the human reaches the requested page.

post.summary: Recommend plugins in a conversation
post.description: Resolves real catalog plugins and publishes durable, actionable plugin cards in the specified channel, thread, or direct message. This does not install or authorize a plugin.

post.summary: Install a plugin
Request user authorization for a plugin

get.description: Returns every Git project attached to this workspace, with the repository's current state and active isolated agent checkouts. Projects you cannot view yet still appear so you can discover their id, but their repository state stays hidden. If a project is not accessible, request access with projects.requestAccess. If the list is empty, publish a connect card with projects.recommend instead of asking the user to paste a URL in chat.

post.summary: Ask the user to connect a Git repository
post.description: Publishes a durable connect-repository card in the current channel, thread, or direct message. Use this when the workspace has no Git project yet instead of asking the user to paste a URL in chat. This does not clone or attach a repository.

post.summary: Inspect a project's branches, status, and recent commits
Create an isolated Git checkout for this agent
post.description: Creates a dedicated branch in a Chief-owned worktree. Make all repository edits there rather than changing the user's attached checkout.

post.summary: Inspect an isolated checkout's changes
Commit this agent's checkout changes
post.description: Stages and commits changes only inside the caller's isolated checkout. The commit is attributed to the agent via Chief and is not pushed or merged.

post.summary: Release a clean isolated checkout
post.description: Removes the worktree only after all changes are committed. It does not delete the branch or its commits.

post.summary: Compare two branches with a bounded diff
post.description: Returns merge status, commit list, and a bounded combined diff between a base and compare ref. Inspect this before publishing work.

post.summary: Publish one owned branch through the trusted credential flow
post.description: Pushes the caller's branch to its Git remote with an explicit refspec. Publishing to the default branch is disabled unless an operator explicitly authorizes it.

post.summary: Discard uncommitted checkout changes after confirmation
post.description: Permanently removes uncommitted and untracked changes inside the caller's isolated checkout. Requires explicit confirmation.

post.summary: Create a provider pull request when the provider supports it
post.description: Creates a pull request from headBranch to baseBranch. Returns a typed unsupported response for repositories without pull request support.

post.summary: Read checks and review state for a provider pull request
post.description: Returns a typed unsupported response for repositories without pull request support.

post.summary: Request all required project scopes in one approval
post.description: Request every scope needed for the intended work at once using capabilities, for example {"projectId":"project-id","capabilities":["view","checkout","commit"]}. Valid scopes are view, checkout, commit, publish, review, and administer. Scopes are cumulative, so approval is stored as the highest requested scope and includes every scope below it. The request stays pending until a workspace operator approves or denies it; nothing is granted automatically. After approval, retry the blocked operation.
